facility.name: Texas Kids Childcare
facility.programs_provided: School Age Care,Before School Care,Meals Provided ,After School Care,Snacks Provided,Transportation to/from School ,Field Trips

inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Parental Notification of Infestation: Based on the preponderance of evidence, there is sufficient evidence to support that the operation did not notify the parents when there was an outbreak of lice.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Notification of Infestation (26 TAC §746.307(e))

occurrences.finding: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children: The toddler classroom had one caregiver to 10 children ni care. The specified age group (SAG) was 20 months. The director made changes and moved the children to a classroom that had less children in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1601)

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Immunizations: There was one child's record that lacked the updated immunization record for the age of the child.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Immunizations (26 TAC §746.603(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Education Outside of U.S.: Three caregivers' personnel file had the educational documents translated to English; however, they lacked the U.S. education equivalent on file.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Education Outside of U.S. (26 TAC §746.1045)

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Vision and Hearing Screening: One child's admission record that met the requirement lacked a vision and hearing screening in the file.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Vision and Hearing Screening (26 TAC §746.603(a)(6))

occurrences.finding: Education Outside of U.S.: Three caregivers' personnel file lacked the translation and U.S. education equivalent on file.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Education Outside of U.S. (26 TAC §746.1045)

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Immunizations: There were 4 children's records that lacked the updated immunization record for the age of the child.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Immunizations (26 TAC §746.603(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months: The annual fire inspection had not been conducted.  The last annual fire inspection was last conducted on 08/31/2023.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months (26 TAC §746.5101(a))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Enrollment Agreement: Two children's admission forms used were outdated. The admission forms do not capture the required minimum standards changes of March 2023.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Enrollment Agreement (26 TAC §746.603(a)(1))

occurrences.finding: Arrangement of Napping Equipment - Provides Access to Walkway: There were 2 classrooms which had the cots arranged with no space for the caregiver and the children to walk in between. This was corrected during the inspection when the director and caregivers moved the cots.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Arrangement of Napping Equipment - Provides Access to Walkway (26 TAC §746.2909(4))

occurrences.finding: Required Admission Information - Special School-age Permissions: Two children's records lacked the school age information.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Admission Information - School Information for School-age Child (26 TAC §746.605(14))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments -  Associated with Food, Naps, or Toilet Training: During an investigation, it was determined that the method that the caregiver reached and placed the children on the cot was inappropriate.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments -  Associated with Food, Naps, or Toilet Training (26 TAC §746.2805(2))

occurrences.finding: Administrative and clerical duties that take caregiver's attention away from children: The caregiver was working on paperwork. It was during nap/rest period, and most all of the children were awake.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Administrative and clerical duties that take caregiver's attention away from children (26 TAC §746.1203(3)(A))

occurrences.finding: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk: Based on the preponderance of evidence gathered, there is sufficient evidence to determine a child was left unsupervised on the playground which was not reported to Child Care Regulation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: Based on the preponderance of evidence gathered, there is sufficient evidence to determine a child was left unsupervised on the playground.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk: Based on the preponderance of evidence, there is sufficient evidence to determine a child was left unsupervised on the playground without parental notification on the day of the incident.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk (26 TAC §746.307(b)(4))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments -  Associated with Food, Naps, or Toilet Training: During an investigation, it was determined that the method that the caregiver reached and placed the children on the cot was inappropriate.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments -  Associated with Food, Naps, or Toilet Training (26 TAC §746.2805(2))

occurrences.finding: Administrative and clerical duties that take caregiver's attention away from children: The caregiver was working on paperwork. It was during nap/rest period, and most all of the children were awake.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Administrative and clerical duties that take caregiver's attention away from children (26 TAC §746.1203(3)(A))

occurrences.finding: Using, Storing and Disposing of Hazardous Materials: Based on the preponderance of evidence, there is sufficient evidence that a caregiver sprayed a fragrance product in the air above the children while the children were napping in a classroom which caused an irritation in a child's eye.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Using, Storing and Disposing of Hazardous Materials (26 TAC §746.3407(13))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Immunizations: There were three children's records that lacked the updated immunization record for their current age.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Immunizations (26 TAC §746.603(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days: There were four infants that lacked the updated written feeding instructions from the parent.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days (26 TAC §746.2421(b))

occurrences.finding: Employee Handwashing After Removing Gloves: A caregiver did not wash hands after removing the glove.  This was corrected at the inspection when the inspector pointed it out. The caregiver washed her hands.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Employee Handwashing After Removing Gloves (26 TAC §746.3415(13))

occurrences.finding: Employee Handwashing After Removing Gloves: A caregiver did not wash hands after removing the glove and replacing it with a new one.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Employee Handwashing After Removing Gloves (26 TAC §746.3415(13))

occurrences.finding: Food Service and Preparation Requirement - Use Sanitary Holders: The caregiver in Infant 3 classroom was providing the infants the snacks on their hands.  The process continued after each infant ate it and reached out for more. This was corrected during the inspection when the inspector stopped the method of serving. The caregiver placed a napkin down on the table and placed the snack on it for the children to reach and eat it.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Food Service and Preparation Requirement - Use Sanitary Holders (26 TAC §746.3317(6))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Health Statement: Two children's files required the health statement from a health care professional.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Health Statement (26 TAC §746.603(a)(3))

occurrences.finding: Additional Minimum Qualifications for Caregivers - HS Diploma, Equivalent, Certification of Completion: Two caregivers did not have the educational qualifications on file. One caregivers document was received during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Additional Minimum Qualifications for Caregivers - HS Diploma, Equivalent, Certification of Completion (26 TAC §746.1107(2))

occurrences.finding: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Infant Feeding Instructions: Eight infants did not have the updated written infant feeding instructions. The instructions last signed by a parent were some in August and others in September.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Infant Feeding Instructions (26 TAC §746.801(2))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Immunizations: Nine children's files lacked the updated immunization record.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Immunizations (26 TAC §746.603(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: The operation staff lacked judgment when it leased a dunk tank that was set on concrete with no other safety precautions taken.  In addition, a substance was used on the slip n slide to create bubbles.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Arrangement of Napping Equipment - Not Blocking Entrances or Exits: There was a crib in infant 3 classroom that was blocking the door.  This was corrected at inspection when the crib was moved away from the door.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Arrangement of Napping Equipment - Not Blocking Entrances or Exits (26 TAC §746.2909(1))

occurrences.finding: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children: Infant 3 had 6 infants in care with 1 caregiver. The specified age group (SAG) was 14 months.  Toddler 1 had 14 children in care with 2 caregivers.  The SAG was 17 months.  Both classrooms had 1 child over the child/caregiver ratio.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1601)

occurrences.finding: Provide Access to Children's Records - Parents: The parent's name was on the admission form. The parent was not provided access to the child's records when requested.   It was provided after further documentation was received by the operation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Provide Access to Children's Records - Parents (26 TAC §746.601(b))

occurrences.finding: Operational Policies - Inform Parents That They May Visit Center Anytime During Operating Hours: The operational policies state the parents must obtain management approval to enter the classrooms.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Operational Policies - Inform Parents That They May Visit Center Anytime During Operating Hours (26 TAC §746.501(b)(1))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Free of other activities: A caregiver in care of a group of children on the playground was seen using personal cell phone.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Free of other activities (26 TAC §746.1203(6))
